title: Practice 5: Perfective or imperfective? The prefixed verbs in use

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: She has already left the office.
exercises.why: **ушла** is the past tense (feminine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **уходила** is imperfective (**уходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: It hasn't come to that yet.
exercises.why: **дошло** is the past tense (neuter) of **дойти** (to go to, to come to, to arrive at, to reach; to come down to) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доходить**. past: он дошёл · она дошла́ · оно дошло́ · они дошли́. — Wiktionary, «дойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Танки дошли до леса.» (Perfective, past) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Когда вы дойдёте до почты, поверните направо.» (future) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choice: **доходило** is imperfective (**доходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: She gave me a ride home.
exercises.why: **довезла** is the past tense (feminine) of **довезти** (to take (to), to carry (as far as, to), to bring (to, as far as)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **довозить**. past: он довёз · она довезла́ · оно довезло́ · они довезли́. — Wiktionary, «довезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **довозила** is imperfective (**довозить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The airplane went into a spin.
exercises.why: **вошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **войти** (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **входить**. past: он вошёл · она вошла́ · оно вошло́ · они вошли́. — Wiktionary, «войти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я вошёл в комнату и открыл окно.» (Perfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я войду в комнату и открою окно.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choice: **входил** is imperfective (**входить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **ушёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **уходил** is imperfective (**уходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: A cat came out from under the desk.
exercises.why: **вылез** is the past tense (masculine) of **вылезть** (to get out, to climb out, to get off; (of hair) to fall out, to come out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вылезать**. past: он вы́лез · она вы́лезла · оно вы́лезло · они вы́лезли. — Wiktionary, «вылезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **вылезал** is imperfective (**вылезать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: She got off her bike.
exercises.why: **слезла** is the past tense (feminine) of **слезть** (to come down, to get down (from), to dismount (from); (colloquial) to come down) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **слезать**. past: он сле́з · она сле́зла · оно сле́зло · они сле́зли. — Wiktionary, «слезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **слезала** is imperfective (**слезать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Who led sheep here?
exercises.why: **привёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **привести** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **приводил** is imperfective (**приводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The ship set sail for Bombay.
exercises.why: **отплыл** is the past tense (masculine) of **отплыть** (to swim away; to sail off) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отплывать**. past: он отплы́л · она отплыла́ · оно отплы́ло · они отплы́ли. — Wiktionary, «отплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. exercises.q: I converted to Christianity.
exercises.why: **перешёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **перейти** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переходить**. past: он перешёл · она перешла́ · оно перешло́ · они перешли́. — Wiktionary, «перейти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. exercises.q: Are you in debt yet?
exercises.why: **влез** is the past tense (masculine) of **влезть** (to get into (something, also figurative), to climb into, to scramble into; to fit in, to go in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **влезать**. past: он вле́з · она вле́зла · оно вле́зло · они вле́зли. — Wiktionary, «влезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **влезал** is imperfective (**влезать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Adriano retired.
exercises.why: **ушел** is the past tense (masculine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **уходил** is imperfective (**уходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I dropped her off at the airport.
exercises.why: **довёз** is the past tense (masculine) of **довезти** (to take (to), to carry (as far as, to), to bring (to, as far as)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **довозить**. past: он довёз · она довезла́ · оно довезло́ · они довезли́. — Wiktionary, «довезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **довозил** is imperfective (**довозить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
